anti_overlap: Defer strain-relief and inspection calibration to fd-lehr-anneal-strain
decision_lens: Is a Break receipt like a geyser eruption (a discrete event whose count over a window means little without the inter-event-interval distribution) or like a continuous tilt reading (a rate signal whose variance over the window is the actual evidence) — and is the v6 spec implicitly choosing one when its underlying phenomenon is the other?
distance_rationale: A non-anthropic geophysical phenomenon at sub-decadal timescales whose entire forecasting literature is built around the relationship between discrete eruption events and the continuous reservoir record that both produces and predicts them.
expected_isomorphisms: Eruption-as-discrete-event maps onto Break-as-gate; reservoir-pressure-tilt-and-tremor record maps onto Break-as-continuous-mode; the hydrothermal observation discipline of recording both and using the latter to forecast the former maps directly onto the question of whether the lifecycle should require both representations or pick one.
focus: Discrete eruption events embedded in continuous reservoir-pressure dynamics, and the forecasting discipline of distinguishing precursors from noise
name: fd-geyser-recurrence
persona: Apply the perspective of a Yellowstone hydrothermal observatory geophysicist studying conduit-driven geysers — they care about the relationship between continuous reservoir-temperature and seismicity records and the discrete eruption events that punctuate them, the difference between a geyser whose interval is metronomic (Old Faithful) and one whose interval is heteroscedastic (Steamboat), the precursor signals that distinguish a real eruption from a degassing burp, and the forecasting trade-off between waiting for a clear gate event versus reading the continuous tilt-and-tremor record, measure inter-eruption-interval variance and precursor-to-eruption lead time, and flag when systems describe a phenomenon as gated (discrete eruption) when its forecastability lives in the continuous record, or vice versa.
review_areas: Whether the ≥N receipts threshold encodes both event count and inter-receipt interval, or whether a pillar with N evenly-spaced receipts is treated identically to one with N clustered receipts
Whether the rate-as-Tier-2-evidence framing addresses the heteroscedasticity problem (some pillars will surface receipts in bursts and others as steady drizzle) or implicitly assumes Poisson
Whether Interspect-scored severity functions as a precursor signal (read continuously, weighted by recency) or only as a gate-event annotation
Whether the Compound window length is calibrated to the natural inter-receipt-interval of healthy pillars, or chosen by convenience and risking false-positive transition either direction

Whether the lifecycle addresses the dormant-geyser case — a pillar whose self-observation has gone silent for legitimate reasons (steady-state operation) vs one whose silence is degraded self-observation
Whether the proposal forecasts the next Break receipt at all, or only reacts to its arrival — and whether forecast-vs-actual divergence is itself trust evidence

severity_examples.condition: Self-observation health is fundamentally a rate signal but the lifecycle reduces it to a count threshold, losing the variance information that distinguishes healthy from degraded pillars
severity_examples.scenario: Gate semantics applied to a continuous-rate phenomenon

severity_examples.condition: A genuinely-stable pillar with low contradiction-rate is treated identically to a pillar whose self-observation has gone blind
Receipts are recorded as they arrive but never forecast; forecast error is not used as additional evidence
severity_examples.scenario: No precursor model for Break-receipt arrival

source_domain: Hydrothermal-system geophysics — geyser eruption dynamics and precursor monitoring at Yellowstone, Geysir, El Tatio
success_hints: Look for inter-receipt-interval distribution requirements, not just count thresholds
Check whether the spec addresses heteroscedasticity across pillar types
See whether dormancy has a defined treatment distinct from degradation
Note whether Break-rate is a forecastable quantity with a residual signal
task_context: Reviewing the §7.1 Break-phase decision in Sylveste vision v6 through the lens of geyser-eruption forecasting. Goal: identify whether the lifecycle is choosing an event semantics for a phenomenon whose forecastable structure lives in the continuous record.
